text:
59 mins: Brighton have put in countless low crosses today. None of them have really worked; it’s been clearance after clearance from Ajayi and Mendy in the Hull backline.
Gourna-Douath goes into the book for a cynical tackle.

Key events
58 mins: The longer this remains goalless, the more you think Hull might fancy nicking all three points. Belloumi does well to dart inside off the right and arrow goalwards, but Verbruggen is equal to the shot.
56 mins: Thomas sends in a decent cross from the left, but Brighton clear and quickly counter … and Rutter decides to pass rather than shoot at the crucial moment.
Probably a case of overplaying it, there, as Gross also tried to lay it off and Hull scrambled it away.
55 mins: The Sky Sports commentators are already joking about Tzolakis being awarded the player of the match prize. There’s still a LONG time remaining for Brighton to find a way past him, guys …
53 mins: 12 shots, six on target, no goals. Hull’s goal is living a charmed existence this afternoon.
Another big chance missed by Gomez! This is really, really close. He brought it down so nicely with a cushioned touch, then from an acute angle he fired inches wide.
How many opportunities do Brighton actually need to score?
51 mins: What Hull have been able to do in this game is keep Pascal Gross quiet, largely nullifying his threat, keeping him closely marked … as I say that the German is able to unleash a left-footed shot, but it’s a fairly routine save from Tzolakis.
50 mins: Dunk strides forward into midfield and his deflected through-ball almost spun kindly for Rutter.
Then, Gomez continues to find space on the Brighton right but his cross is missed completely by the onrushing Ayari. A complete air shot.
48 mins: Brighton opted not to make a change at half-time, but I wonder how long it will be before Hürzeler calls upon the likes of Hinshelwood, Minteh and Kostoulas from his bench, which is pretty stacked talent-wise.
46 mins: And Thomas is straight into the action, pressing Costinha and winning Hull a throw-in.
Daniel Sturridge has just described modern day shin-pads as “sim card sized” on Sky Sports, which is phenomenal I must say. Sorba Thomas is sporting a super-small pair on his legs.
Back under way for the second half! Let’s have some goals, please …
Sorba Thomas is on for Hull, replacing Mohamed-Ali Cho, so a like-for-like change out wide by Sergej Jakirović.
Hull at home in the Premier League this season:
- Hull 2-0 Manchester United
- Hull 0-0 Aston Villa
- Hull 2-2 Everton
- Hull 1-1 Brentford
- Hull 2-2 Ipswich
- Hull 0-0 Brighton (HT)
“Drawn with the Tigers, you’re getting drawn by … “
Not everyone is enjoy this game as much as me, it appears.
Mary Waltz emails in: “Dom, greetings from California. It’s still dark here and the early start was not a problem. But I am struggling to stay awake watching this match.”
It does need a goal, Mary, I will admit that.
Konstantinos Tzolakis was no doubt the hero of that half for Hull. The data tells us that Brighton fashioned chances worth 1.75 expected goals across 10 shots, five of which were on target.
Fabian Hürzeler will scarcely believe his team haven’t scored, yet he and his staff must find answers after the break.
Time for me to grap a cuppa and some more Pringles (other oddly-shaped crisps are available).
Brighton should be 1-0 up at half-time – and they carved out possibly their best and clearest chance on the brink of the whistle. Gomez ran onto the cross from the left, drilling low and hard, but somehow Konstantinos Tzolakis got something in the way of it and it deflected out for a corner.
Pascal Gross thinks he was fouled in the buildup to that chance, but both Peter Bankes and VAR have dismissed his appeals. Phew … what a flurry of activity just before the break. After all that it’s finished goalless after the first 45 minutes.
45 mins +2: One underrated and less heralded aspect of Brighton’s game in how aggressive and physical they are. I feel like they have stood up to the physical challenge posed by Hull and imposed themselves on the game, before getting on the ball to strut their stuff.
The Seagulls are trying to fashion a chance late in the first half, right now …
Three added minutes. Brighton would love a breakthrough here.
44 mins: I say it’s been a gruelling half for Hull … but the home fans will be delighted with their team’s commitment and focus.
There’s a blow here for them, though. Tim Iroegbunam is going to be forced off with an injury. A replay of the challenge that caused the problem is quite tough to watch, a really nasty one as Iroegbunam clashed with Chema Andres.
Gourna-Douath is going to come on, he’s receiving instructions now.
I cannot see a foul in that melee – play on. Hull certainly are making the most of the set-piece opportunities they are getting, though. McBurnie is doing a great job drawing fouls from Vuskovic and Lewis Dunk.
41 mins: Verbruggen sprawls across his goal to make sure Belloumi’s free-kick does not sneak in. Hull then have a couple of crossing opportunities and start to get physical, amid halfhearted appeals for a home penalty.
Some positive moments for the Tigers towards the end of a gruelling half.
39 mins: Brighton could and possibly should have scored two or three already.
Hull will not care one bit. McBurnie has won another free-kick from the frustrated Vuskovic. The young Seagulls centre-back is getting a different kind of challenge at the MKM Stadium today.
Off the woodwork from Ayari! He met Gomez’s cutback with a sweet right-footed shot … and then Rutter is denied by another Tzolakis save from close range. A really big double chance for Brighton. Tzolakis and the frame of the goal are both proving hard to get past.
36 mins: McBurnie makes a nuisance of himself to win a corner for Hull and the crowd respond to his efforts with a roar.
It’s a damp squib in the end, however, as Verbruggen gets some catching practice from the resulting kick.
34 mins: It’s (more) bad news for my FPL team as Vuskovic kicks the ball away after fouling Cho and gets a booking for his troubles.
33 mins: Rutter isn’t a regular starter for Brighton, especially not in the No 9 position and I wonder whether the Seagulls are missing having an out-and-out striker. Rutter, Gomez, Gross and Ayari … they all kind of prefer playing in the pocket. Maybe a focal point would benefit Brighton instead.
32 mins: Cho gets a rare opportunity to run at Costinha and gets in a cross with his left foot, which Matt Crooks tries to flick from behind him. Unfortunately for Hull, Crooks cannot get any power on the flick and it’s straight at Verbruggen.
Tzolakis parries from Rutter at the other end, another smart save from the Hull stopper.
30 mins: Hull really aren’t having much of the ball. Even when they do, it’s pumped long quite swiftly.
28 mins: A well co-ordinated press from Hull has Verbruggen and his defenders worrying for a moment, hurriedly squirrelling the ball into touch, which allows another long throw from the hosts. Mendy hooks it tamely at the Brighton goal, and Verbruggen collects.
26 mins: If Hull versus Brighton feels strange as a top flight game, that’s because this is the first time they’ve ever met in the Premier League.
Fabian Hürzeler will not be panicking on the touchline, despite the goalless scoreline. His team’s general dominance will be his overriding thought.
